Thanksgiving Foods You Can Safely Share With Your Dog

Want to include your dog in the Thanksgiving feast? Here are the holiday foods you can safely share with your pup—and the ones to keep off their plate.

Last Updated: November 23, 2026

Share:
Read Caption
Photo credit: FamVeld/Shutterstock
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:56
Instaread

Thanksgiving is all about gathering around the table and enjoying a big meal—and it’s only natural to want your four-legged family member to join in. The good news? There are several Thanksgiving staples you can safely share with your dog. Here’s what can make it onto their plate, and what should stay off it.

ilona.shorokhova/shutterstock

Thanksgiving Foods You Can Share With Your Dog

#1 Turkey

Towfiqu ahamed barbhuiya/shutterstock

Plain, fully cooked, boneless, skinless turkey meat. No seasoning, gravy, or fatty skin.

#2 Sweet Potatoes

New Africa/shutterstock

Cooked and served plain, without butter, sugar, marshmallows, or spices, sweet potatoes are a great, healthy treat for dogs.

#3 Green Beans

Tetiana Tychynska/shutterstock

Plain, cooked or steamed green beans are a nice low-calorie treat.

#4 Pumpkin

New Africa/shutterstock

Plain pumpkin puree (not pumpkin pie filling) can be a tasty treat.

#5 Carrots

New Africa/shutterstock

Cooked or raw, cut into appropriately sized pieces.

#6 Peas

MarcoFood/shutterstock

Plain peas without butter, salt, or seasoning.

#7 Apples

Nataly Studio/shutterstock

A few seedless, core-free apple slices make a crunchy treat for dogs.

Foods to keep away from your dog

  • Stuffing: Often contains onion, garlic, raisins, or other unsafe ingredients.
  • Gravy: Usually too fatty and salty; may contain onion and garlic.
  • Mashed potatoes: Often loaded with butter, cream, salt, and garlic.
  • Turkey bones: Can splinter and cause choking or internal injuries.
  • Onions and garlic: Toxic to dogs.
  • Grapes and raisins: Can cause kidney injury.
  • Chocolate desserts: Toxic to dogs.
  • Xylitol-sweetened desserts: Extremely dangerous to dogs.

Happy Thanksgiving everyone!
